hints.content:
$h$ is decreasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $h(x)$ decreases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going downwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of y equals h of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through negative five, forty and the x-intercept negative four, zero. The function continues to decrease until the local minimum at negative two and one-half, negative twenty-five. Then it increases through the origin until the local maximum at two and one-half, twenty five. The function then decreases again through the x-intercept four, zero and goes through the point five, negative forty. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative five to x equals negative two and one-half and from x equals two and one-half to five.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $h$ decreasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-4<x<-3$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$-2<x<0$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $h$ is increasing on this interval
$0<x<2$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $h$ is increasing on this interval
